notes: GPT-6 Sol/Luna launch-post effort x cost curves, parsed from the launch page's public Next.js hydration payload (11 vegaLiteSpec objects inside self.__next_f.push chunks) as exact JSON — NOT chart digitization. Every row is VENDOR-published (evidence_grade C) even where the benchmark carries a third-party name (AutomationBench, FrontierCode, DeepSWE, OSWorld): the publisher of these particular numbers is OpenAI. All six effort-stratified curves use x=cost (field 'cost', axis title 'Cost per task', USD, log-scale) and y=score (field 'score', a 0-1 fraction; axis title 'Score' on four charts, 'Answers with any factual error' on the fifth) — there is NO time/latency series on this launch page (unlike the GPT-6 Astra launch page's latency_s-keyed chart, which held minutes for one chart and an unconfirmed unit for another; see performance/openai-gpt-6-astra-launch-2026-09.json). The five 'lower is better' bar charts (coding deception, broken-search non-disclosure, Codex reviewer-bypass attempts, warning circumvention, unauthorized message-board action) are single-point-per-model adversarial safety evals, NOT effort x cost curves — they carry no 'cost' field at all. Only two of the five bar charts' captions verbatim state 'Effort was set to maximum' (coding deception; broken-search-tool non-disclosure); the other three (reviewer bypass, warning circumvention, unauthorized agent interaction) do NOT state an effort level in their caption, so 'effort' is omitted from those rows rather than assumed max — do not backfill it from the sibling charts. GPT-5.6 Luna's 'Unauthorized agent interaction' point is explicitly labeled 'Not measured' in the source data (scoreLabel field) and is recorded only in missing[], never as score:0 or any other invented value. Two comparison models appear only as fallback-composite series, kept under their base catalog id with a row-level caveat rather than a new model id: 'Claude Fable 5.1 w/ Opus 5 Fallback' -> claude-fable-5-1 (AutomationBench caption states this datapoint UNDERSTATES actual cost — it omits the ~40%-of-tasks Opus 5 fallback cost); 'Claude Fable 5 w/ Opus 4.8 fallback' / bare 'Claude Fable 5' -> claude-fable-5 (DeepSWE and Agents' Last Exam charts). gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna are NOT YET in models.json as of this document's commit (a separate catalog-registry workstream owns that L0 registry entry); scripts/validate_data_pack.py is expected to fail model-id resolution for gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna until that lane lands, per this pack's usual multi-worker sequencing (see the Opus 5.5 digitized-curves precedent, performance/anthropic-opus5-5-digitized-2026-09.json, which shipped under the same constraint). Series coverage is NOT uniform across charts — this mirrors what the launch page itself shows, not an extraction gap: only AutomationBench, Agents' Last Exam, FrontierCode, and DeepSWE include a Claude comparison model at all; 'Factual error rate on difficult prompts' and 'OSWorld 2.0, offline set' cover only the five OpenAI models (no Claude series at all on the OSWorld chart; Claude Opus 5 only, no Fable, on OSWorld). Point-count integrity: every one of the 213 raw data points across all 11 vegaLiteSpec objects is accounted for — 212 recorded as scores[] rows, 1 recorded in missing[] (the GPT-5.6 Luna 'Not measured' point) — verified by an automated count (scripts run: total vegaLiteSpec values == len(scores) + len(missing)); no silent drops. Cross-check: the one chart whose SVG was present in the raw fetched HTML (AutomationBench) was independently cross-validated against the page's 38 rendered aria-label point strings (31 unique points + 7 duplicated first-points per series == 38); all 31 AutomationBench vegaLiteSpec points match their corresponding aria-label cost/score values exactly. The other 10 charts were not yet client-rendered as SVG in this fetch (no aria-label list exists for them in the captured HTML), so their evidence rests solely on the hydration payload; see charts-report.md for the full point-count diff.

In our internal coding deception evaluation, AI agents are given tasks deliberately selected to elicit dishonesty. In typical usage, deception is much rarer. Deception rate measures the fraction of answers with any detected deception. Effort was set to maximum.

In Codex, an automated safety reviewer can block a command it judges unsafe and tell the model not to retry the action or something similar. We tested whether models respect that decision or try to work around it. GPT-6 Sol made no observed attempts to bypass the decision. GPT-6 Luna attempted to do so in 0.3% of runs, down from 4.3% for GPT-5.6 Luna, with no successful bypasses observed. Effort level is NOT stated in this chart's caption/source (unlike the coding-deception and broken-search-tool charts on the same page, which state 'Effort was set to maximum'); do not assume max.

We tested whether models followed unauthorized instructions on a simulated message board, such as requests to disclose private information. Among runs in which models found the board, GPT-6 Sol took the specified unauthorized action in 11% of cases, compared with 52% for GPT-5.6 Sol. No such actions were observed for GPT-6 Luna or Astra, although Luna found the board less often. These deliberately adversarial results do not represent typical use.
